question: Nursing informatics is a blend of three major fields. Which ones are they?

options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics brings together patient care, computers, and data management to make healthcare smoother and safer for everyone. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main reason we use computers and digital tools in clinical nursing?

options.A: To make healthcare delivery safer and more efficient
options.B: To reduce the number of registered nurses needed in a hospital
options.C: To eliminate all verbal communication among healthcare team members
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical bedside nursing assessments

explanation: You got it! Technology is there to back you up as a nurse—reducing mistakes and saving time—not to take away your vital human touch. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: To automatically prescribe medications without a doctor's order
options.B: To track the daily attendance and payroll of hospital staff
options.C: To store a comprehensive digital history of a patient's health information
options.D: To manage the public financial budget of the hospital

explanation: Correct! An EHR keeps all of a patient's medical history, test results, and treatments in one digital folder so authorized health workers can see them easily. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is 'system interoperability' such a big deal when hospitals share patient records?

options.A: It stops nurses from making any type of documentation error
options.B: It allows different health departments and facilities to share patient data smoothly
options.C: It ensures that all hospitals use the exact same brand of computer hardware
options.D: It prevents patients from viewing their own medical test results online

explanation: Exactly! Interoperability simply means different computer systems can talk to each other, so patient information travels safely between labs, clinics, and hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: How do handheld barcode scanners help keep patients safe right at the bedside?

options.A: They help verify the right patient and the right medication before giving drugs
options.B: They allow patients to scan and self-administer their own prescription drugs
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for nurses to check vital signs manually
options.D: They automatically calculate the hospital bill for the patient

explanation: Spot on! Scanning the patient's wristband and the drug package acts as a final safety check to make sure the right medicine goes to the right person. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: You are about to give an IV antibiotic to your patient. What is the best way to use technology right at that moment?

options.A: Leave the medication at the bedside table while going to find a laptop
options.B: Write the administration time on a piece of paper to type into the desktop computer later
options.C: Scan the patient identification band and the medication label using a handheld device
options.D: Ask a family member to double-check the medication order on the wall chart

explanation: You nailed it! Point-of-care scanning right at the bedside prevents errors and ensures your charting is accurate in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of remote patient monitoring tools?

options.A: To track patient health metrics from a distance and alert nurses to dangerous changes
options.B: To broadcast educational health videos on community television channels
options.C: To monitor hospital inventory levels and surgical equipment supplies
options.D: To replace all in-person physical therapy sessions for recovering patients

explanation: Correct! Remote tools let patients check vital signs at home so nurses can spot warning signs early, even from miles away. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: How do telehealth and home monitoring devices truly help patients living with chronic illnesses?

options.A: By lowering the financial cost of purchasing digital home appliances
options.B: By removing the need for patients to ever speak with a doctor again
options.C: By curing chronic diseases without the need for any prescription medications
options.D: By catching early warning signs before they turn into major emergencies

explanation: Spot on! Keeping a close eye on daily trends helps the care team step in before a small issue becomes a full-blown crisis. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To legally sign medical documents on behalf of busy attending physicians
options.B: To order hospital kitchen meals based on patient dietary preferences
options.C: To schedule nursing shift rotations and manage monthly hospital payrolls
options.D: To provide automated prompts and guidelines that assist clinicians in making safe choices

explanation: You got it! CDSS software acts like a smart assistant, analyzing patient data to give helpful alerts and evidence-based tips. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a Clinical Decision Support System in action?

options.A: The computer screen automatically dims to save electricity during night shift hours
options.B: An email reminder is sent to the nurse manager about an upcoming staff meeting
options.C: A pop-up warning appears on the screen noting that a newly ordered drug conflicts with a patient allergy
options.D: A printer in the nurse's station prints out the morning breakfast menu list

explanation: Spot on! Drug-allergy alerts are a great example of CDSS protecting patients by catching potential mistakes before they reach the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: As a nurse using hospital technology, which of the following is NOT your job?

options.A: Writing the core computer programming code for the hospital software
options.B: Protecting patient privacy and maintaining strict confidentiality
options.C: Following secure password and login protocols at every shift
options.D: Providing practical feedback on how easy a clinical software tool is to use

explanation: Correct! Software coding is left to the IT experts. Nurses focus on safe clinical use, patient privacy, and giving feedback on how well the tools work. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is it so important for hospitals to ask nurses for their opinion when buying new software?

options.A: Hospital administrators are not allowed to buy software without nursing financial approval
options.B: Nurses are legally required to purchase the hardware equipment for the hospital
options.C: Nurses understand the practical bedside workflow and can spot usability issues that affect safety
options.D: Nurses are the only staff members permitted to touch computers in the building

explanation: You nailed it! Because nurses know how care actually flows at the bedside, their input ensures new technology helps rather than gets in the way. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)
